transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-24
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording ID: ff-2026-06-24-orbitera-0034

Summary:
Quick mid-POC scrub to review the head-to-head latency/throughput numbers vs the incumbent provider, triage higher-than-expected p95 in region eu-west-1, discuss tuning applied (batching, quantization, prefix cache) and agree next steps for a 2-hour load comparison and security handoff.

Topics discussed:
- p50/p95/p99 latency differences and tail behavior
- throughput (QPS) and sustained saturation testing
- unit token cost delta and autoscale impact
- routing/fallback playbook and dedicated slot tradeoffs
- SOC2/KMS/SSO questions from security team

Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect):
[00:00] Evan Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Jordan, thanks for getting the team together, appreciate it. This is Evan from Redwood, Priya is my SE, Samir on CSM. How's everyone?
[00:10] Jordan Lee: Yeah hi uh thanks, we'll try and keep this focused. We've been looking at the bench results you sent last night. A couple surprises around p95 in eu-west, so want to go through that.
[00:18] Priya Shah: Great, yeah we pulled the latest traces — quick caveat the numbers are from the lab cluster, not yet the dedicated slot. We tuned kernel selection and bumped the batcher from 8 to 12 for burst tests which improved throughput but we saw a tail increase on longer contexts.
[00:30] Priya Kumar: Right so our baseline from IncumbentCloudAI in eu-west-1 shows p95 about 320 ms on 256-token requests. Your runs on Monday showed ~210 ms p50 but p95 drifted to 420 ms in one window, that's the main thing we flagged.
[00:44] Priya Shah: Yeah and that 420 spike correlates with KV cache misses during interleaved long-context sessions, uh so prefix cache warming was incomplete. We applied a KV cache persistence tweak last night and re-ran a 30 min soak, that reduced p95 to ~260 ms in the same test.
[01:00] Marcus O'Neal: Can you remind us what quantization profile you used? We saw an earlier note about int8 vs q4_0 changes. The incumbent is using mixed-precision with some custom kernels.
[01:08] Priya Shah: We tested three profiles: fp16 baseline, int8-qat, and q4_0 approximate. The best perf/quality split for your workload was int8-optimized with selective FP16 for attention kernels. That got us better throughput with small quality delta.
[01:20] Jordan Lee: And unit token cost — you said Redwood's unit cost was lower in the row? The spreadsheets show about 18% lower token cost at current batch settings, is that right?
[01:27] Evan Martinez: Correct, on the hosted stack with our autoscaler and prefix caching we see an estimate around 18% lower per-token for the median workload. But we also showed a sensitive case where when tail spikes happen cost delta can compress, so the goal is to stabilize tail.
[01:39] Lina Torres: From security perspective we need KMS integration details, audit log retention, and also SSO/SAML flows. Do you provide customer-managed keys in private deployments?
[01:45] Evan Martinez: Yes — for Private we support KMS/HSM integrations and customer-managed keys. We'll send the security pack and SOC2 snapshot after the call. Note: the managed hosted offering uses encryption at rest with our keys by default but we can present an architecture for VPC + bring-your-own-key.
[02:00] Jordan Lee: Back to performance, can you walk through the p99 noise — is that noisy because of retries or queuing?
[02:06] Priya Shah: p99 was influenced by two things in the lab: scheduled background compactions on the host and some thread preemption during autoscale events. We mitigated the compaction schedule and pinned inference threads in the latest run. Those changes cut p99 outliers by ~30%.
[02:20] Priya Kumar: Did you also test with longer tokens — 1k tokens versus 256? Our chat-summary workflows often hit 800-1k tokens which impacts KV cache and memory layout.
[02:28] Priya Shah: Yes, we ran a few long context tests. For 1k token sequences, p95 increases as expected; however with our prefix caching optimization and continuous batching the throughput stays linear until about 1.2k tokens after which memory pressure causes fragmentation. We recommended using dynamic eviction thresholds for your workload.
[02:42] Marcus O'Neal: What about routing — do you have a fallback to a cheaper model or region if latency goes above threshold?
[02:47] Evan Martinez: We do — smart routing policy can send traffic to a compatible variant (smaller quantized model) or another region. We also have automatic fallback to our 'low-cost' tier which serves at slightly higher latency but keeps p95 bounded. We'll propose a routing playbook for your SLA.
[03:00] Jordan Lee: On the dedicated slot conversation, how many concurrent slots do you estimate for our 500 QPS steady state?
[03:06] Priya Shah: Rough estimate is 6 dedicated slots on A100-type instances with our current model quantization and the batching profile you saw. If you want a 2x buffer for peak, we recommend 12 slots. We'll put an exact capacity planner in the pricing proposal.
[03:20] Jordan Lee: Fine. Also curious about warm-up times on a cold restart — the incumbent seems to have a faster cold start for some models.
[03:26] Priya Shah: Cold start depends on disk-to-GPU load path and kernel warm-up. We optimized image layering and prefetch so cold start is ~30-45 seconds for the larger model in our lab; the incumbent's number may vary by infra. For steady-state this is less important, but if your workflow has many ephemeral containers we can pre-warm using reserved pools.
[03:40] Lina Torres: For compliance we need audit logs for token-level access and role-based access controls. Is audit retention configurable?
[03:46] Samir Naik: Yes, audit retention is configurable per tenant in Private. Hosted customers currently get 90 days by default, enterprise add-on for 365 days. We'll include the options in the security pack.
[03:58] Jordan Lee: There was a set of ablation tests we wanted — can Redwood run a run that isolates quantization-only impact vs batching-only? We want separate traces to attribute latency/cost differences.
[04:06] Priya Shah: Absolutely, we can provide ablation runs. Proposed plan: two 1-hour windows — quantization-only (no batch size change) and batching-only (no quantization) then combined. We'll tag traces so you can compare directly to the incumbent run.
[04:20] Jordan Lee: Good. We'll need those run configs in advance so our SRE can provision the right traffic.
[04:26] Evan Martinez: We'll share a short runbook with exact endpoints and scripts. Samir will follow up.
[04:32] Priya Kumar: One more on monitoring — can we get token-level cost breakdown by route? We want to see cost per model variant and by region.
[04:38] Samir Naik: Yep, Redwood Console provides per-route and per-model token-level cost and latency breakdowns. We can grant a temporary dashboard view for your SRE during the POC.
[04:46] Jordan Lee: Ok let's make sure the timeline is tight — we'd like the 2-hour head-to-head next Wednesday 06-30 UTC window if possible.
[04:52] Evan Martinez: We'll check resources and confirm by EOD. Priya will run the ablation tests beforehand.
[04:58] Lina Torres: On the KMS and network side, can we do a short lab handshake with your infra team next week? We need to validate VPN connectivity and firewall allow-lists.
[05:06] Evan Martinez: Yes. We'll add a networking slot. We'll also send the security artifact pack.
[05:12] Jordan Lee: Great, thanks — I think that's a wrap.
[05:16] Evan Martinez: Cool, recap quickly: Redwood sends SOC2/security pack and runbook, Priya runs ablation tests and stress run and posts logs, we propose dedicated slot pricing and capacity plan, Orbitera schedules the 2-hour head-to-head next Wed and confirms SLAs. Anything else?
[05:28] Marcus O'Neal: No, that's it from me. Thanks all.
[05:32] Priya Shah: Thanks everyone.

End of recording.
